content.title: Pensacola's Keyla Richardson makes 'American Idol' Top 11
content.text: April 6, 2026Updated April 7, 2026, 12:03 a.m. CTLast week, judges praised Richardson's performance of "Jireh" and her commanding stage presenceFans can vote for Richardson via the show's website, text message and social mediaKeyla Richardson survived another episode of "American Idol," reaching the Top 11.In a second round of eliminations on Monday night, Richardson moved through to the Top 11 based on live voting that took place during the episode.Keyla Richardson makes 'American Idol' Top 12 MondayPensacola “American Idol” contestant Keyla Richardson has earned a place in the “American Idol” Top 12. Now, she will sing again for America's votes to advance to the next level of the competition.Richardson learned her fate in the opening moments of tonight's episode. Voting is already live for the next elimination round, planned for the end of the episode.How to vote for Keyla Richardson on 'American Idol'There are three ways to vote on American Idol — on the American Idol website, over text message, and the newly introduced social media voting method, using Facebook, Instagram and TikTok.Each week, voters may vote 10 times per contestant per method, so each person could cast 50 votes for Richardson across all methods.For voting on the American Idol website, visit AmericanIdol.com/Vote once the voting window opens.For text message voting, text the number of the finalist you would like to vote for to “21523.” Richardson’s voting number will be 20.What else happens tonight on 'American Idol'Now that the Top 12 have been revealed, the remaining contestants will take on the annual Judge’s Song Contest, where each of the judges has chosen a song for the remaining contestants. This year, they will be choosing from '90s hits. The contestants have chosen from their three choices without knowing which judge picked each song. The winning judge will receive a point for the contestant's choice.A live elimination is planned for the end of episode.What happened last week?Last week, Richardson was right in her element for the themed night of “Songs of Faith” and she dazzled judges with a performance of “Jireh” by Elevation Worship and Maverick City Music, featuring Candler Moore and Naomi Raine. Judges called attention not only to her voice but also to her commanding presence on stage.“You were walking that walk, singing that song and I just love your stage presence, and your presentation was so wonderful,” Richie said.“You’ve kind of touched me in a lot of ways since your audition, just watching your growth from there to now, watching you come out here and really command the room and the stage…you’re just making this your moment, and I love that,” judge Luke Bryan said to Richardson. “Way to kick off the night, great job.”When asked about her song choice, Richardson said it stemmed from gratitude to God and for her platform being part of the “American Idol” journey.Not only were the judges impressed with her performance, so was America, as their votes landed her a place in the show's Top 12.Pensacola's community support has Richardson "getting teary-eyed"Before Richardson began American Idol's live performance rounds, she attended a watch party/send-off with family, friends, and fans on March 16 at Andy D’s on Pensacola Bay with her 9-year-old son, Drew.For Richardson, seeing the Pensacola community support her throughout her journey has had her "getting teary-eyed" throughout the season.“Just having a supportive hometown means a lot. … Just seeing them support something positive, it’s everything to me. It really touches my heart," Richardson told the News Journal. "I’ve been getting teary-eyed all the time because that’s all I want to bring, some positive energy and just shed some light.”Her fan-base, the "Keyhive," has reconvened tonight to show Richardson support from afar, gathering again for an organized watch party on April 6 at Margarita's Fusion & Bar to help spur live voting, which will be necessary to carry Richardson into the next stage of the competition.How American Idol’s new social media voting worksIn order to make the most of American Idol’s new social voting, there are some ground rules to understand.Voters need to visit American Idol’s “Official Vote Post,” which will be pinned on each platform, then leave a comment on the post that includes who they are voting for. You can vote up to 10 times per contestant per platform, but all votes must be cast in individual comments.Voters cannot include the names of multiple contestants in one comment, or repeat the name of the same contestant multiple times in one comment.To view the full guidance on voting, visit idolvote.abc.com/#faq.Richardson’s musical journey started in PensacolaRichardson has been singing almost her entire life, starting with singing gospel in Pensacola's churches.“I’ve always had a love for singing. I’ve been singing since the age of 5. I was raised in the church and so I just wanted to do more,” Richardson said. “I felt like I was just in a box and I just wanted to branch out and see what they got in store for me.”She went on to become a music teacher at Life Shifting Learning Academy on Pensacola Boulevard, where she’s been for about six years. She knows what it’s like to need someone to believe in you, and also importantly, to learn to believe in yourself. Now, she works to help young people develop their voices and gets to be the one who believes in them.Now, when Richardson visits her students during the season, she can pass along lots of hugs and a few words of wisdom.“They hug on me, love on me. I have to make them do their work,” Richardson said of her students. “I just want to let the world know, never give up. Always chase your dream, don’t let nobody stop you chasing your dream. You just keep going, no matter what.”Has Richardson been on TV before?Richardson has showcased her voice on television before. She landed in the top four of BET’s “Sunday Best,” which allows aspiring gospel artists to learn from the artists they grew up listening to, to meet peers, and share their talent with a vast new audience.Opportunities only continued to open from there, leading her to claim her first No. 1 on Billboard’s Gospel Airplay for her single “So Good.” She would go on to earn the role of Vicky Waters in the 2022 film “Due Season,” starring alongside actress Vivica A. Fox.However, auditioning for 'American Idol' had long been a dream of hers, and she felt it was time to pursue it. Now, she wants to motivate others to do the same.“The most I’ve taken out of it is just to keep going, even when you don’t feel like it, even if you don’t feel like you can’t do it – you can do it. Anything you put your mind to, I say it all the time, but that’s the thing I took out of it just to keep pushing," Richardson said.When does 'American Idol' come on?ABC airs "American Idol" at 7 p.m. CDT every Monday. If you don't have cable, paid streaming platforms also show episodes in real time, such as YouTube TV, DirecTV, Fubo, Sling, Hulu + Live TV and more. If you missed it, the episode is then available to stream on Hulu the next day
